items.text: A fork is one piece attacking two enemy pieces at once. Here the knight on c7 checks the king and attacks the rook. The king must move, so the rook is lost.

items.prompt: Tap every black piece the knight attacks.
items.explain: The knight on e5 hits the queen on d7, the rook on f7 and the pawn on g6. Knights jump, so nothing can block them.

items.prompt: Move the knight so it attacks the king and the rook at the same time.
items.explain: Knight to c7 checks the king on e8 and attacks the rook on a8 at once. The king has to move, and the knight takes the rook.

items.prompt: True or false: after the knight jumps to f7, it attacks both the king and the queen.
items.explain: From f7 the knight checks the king on h8 and attacks the queen on d8.

items.text: A puzzle starts with the other side's move. Shaded squares show where it went from and to. Then it's your turn.

items.explain: Knight to c7 checks the king and hits the rook on a8. The king has to step away, and the knight takes the rook.
items.prompt: Black moved a pawn. Now find the knight fork.

items.text: Knights fork best. A knight jumps in an L, reaches up to eight squares, and nothing can block it. Here one knight hits the queen and the rook.

items.prompt: Tap every black piece the knight attacks.
items.explain: From e6 the knight hits d8, f8, c5 and g5: four pieces from one square. A knight deep in enemy ground is a fork waiting to happen.

items.prompt: Move the knight so it attacks the king and the queen together.
items.explain: Knight to f7 checks the king on h8 and attacks the queen on d6. The king must deal with the check first, so the queen is lost.

items.prompt: True or false: after the knight jumps to c7, it attacks both rooks.
items.explain: From c7 the knight reaches a8 and e8, but not f8. One rook attacked is a threat, not a fork.
Knight to f6 checks the king and attacks the queen on d5. After the king moves, the knight takes the queen.
items.prompt: Black just moved the queen to d5. Find the fork.

items.explain: Knight to c7 hits the king, the rook on a8 and the queen on a6 at once: a family fork. Whatever Black does, the queen falls.
items.prompt: Black moved the queen to a6. Find a fork that hits three pieces.

items.text: Any piece can fork. A pawn fork hurts most: the cheapest piece on the board attacks two that are worth more. Here the pawn hits a knight and a bishop.

items.prompt: Tap every black piece the pawn attacks.
items.explain: A pawn attacks one square diagonally forward on each side: c6 and e6. The pawn on b6 is on neither, so it's safe.

items.prompt: Move a pawn forward so it attacks both knights.
items.explain: Pawn to d4 attacks the knights on c5 and e5 at once, and neither knight can take it. Black can save only one.

items.prompt: Tap every black piece the queen attacks.
items.explain: From d4 the queen reaches a7, d7, g4 and h8 along her lines. The pawn on h4 is safe behind the one on g4: queens can't jump.

items.prompt: True or false: after the queen moves to e4, she attacks both the king and the rook.
items.explain: From e4 the queen checks the king on h7 along one diagonal and hits the rook on a8 along the other. Black must answer the check, and the rook goes.
Queen to d5 checks the king along one diagonal and attacks the rook on a8 along the other. After the king steps aside, the queen takes the rook.
items.prompt: Black moved the king to g8. Find the queen fork.
